overview: PARoG proposes a Plan-Answer-Refine framework for LLM reasoning on knowledge graphs, using SPARQL-guided structured planning to decompose complex queries into compositional sub-objectives and a plan-answer-refine paradigm to mitigate search space truncation bias and error amplification, evaluated on WebQSP, CWQ, and GrailQA benchmarks.

modules.name: SPARQL Query Parsing and Decomposition
modules.description: Parse SPARQL queries from KGQA datasets into atomic operations and classify them into operation types (conjunctions, compositions, comparatives, superlatives, linear queries). Extract the structural graph-matching patterns and decompose complex queries into consecutive search operations and constraints.

modules.name: Training Data Generation Pipeline
modules.description: Construct large-scale planning training data by collecting Question-SPARQL pairs from WebQSP, GrailQA, and CWQ training splits, then using GPT-4o to perform semantic consistency mapping: decompose SPARQL into atomic operations, translate each into natural language sub-objectives, and rephrase the decomposed sequences back to natural language queries for semantic consistency.

modules.name: Planning Module Training
modules.description: Fine-tune a Llama-3.1-8B backbone on the generated planning data using standard autoregressive language modeling loss, optimizing the negative log-likelihood over sub-objective token sequences. The model learns to map complex natural language questions into structured compositional reasoning plans that mirror SPARQL logic.

modules.name: Knowledge Graph Interface and Query Engine
modules.description: Implement the KG connectivity layer supporting Freebase and WikiData, providing SPARQL query execution, entity neighbor retrieval, relation lookup, and predefined SPARQL query templates for forward and backward entity searches (e.g., (e,r,?) and (?,r,e) patterns).

modules.name: Topic Entity Identification
modules.description: Identify initial topic entities from the input question to seed the KG exploration process, producing the starting entity set E0 for iterative graph traversal.

modules.name: KG Exploration Engine
modules.description: Implement iterative graph exploration starting from topic entities. At each iteration, collect tail entities from current reasoning paths, retrieve their neighbor relations, expand reasoning paths by querying missing entities via SPARQL templates, and update the reasoning path set. Maintain traceability across exploration steps with dynamic beam management.

modules.name: Relation Pruning Module
modules.description: Given the original question, global plan, and all relations connected to tail entities in the current reasoning paths, leverage the LLM to filter out irrelevant relations. The full plan context is provided to maintain awareness of the global reasoning objective and prevent over-focusing on local steps.

modules.name: Entity Scoring and Selection
modules.description: Score candidate entities retrieved during KG exploration by computing their relevance to the current sub-objective and the overall question using the LLM, then select the most relevant entities to update reasoning paths while maintaining a dynamic selection strategy rather than fixed top-k.

modules.name: Initial Answer Generation
modules.description: For each sub-objective in the generated plan, use the LLM's parametric knowledge to produce a tentative answer independently, serving as the baseline before KG evidence integration. This decouples LLM internal knowledge from external retrieval to reduce over-reliance on retrieved facts.

modules.name: Self-Refinement Module
modules.description: After each KG exploration iteration, re-evaluate the tentative answer against retrieved evidence triples. If inconsistencies or supplementary information are detected, refine the answer by adjusting entities or relations. If retrieved knowledge does not align with the question, fall back to the parametric tentative answer. This explicit integration of parametric and external knowledge mitigates error amplification.

modules.name: Plan-Answer-Refine Orchestrator
modules.description: Implement the main algorithmic loop that coordinates the planning module, initial answering, iterative KG exploration, and self-refinement for each sub-objective. Includes stopping criteria: check whether the refined result is sufficient to answer the overall question, and enforce a maximum iteration limit to avoid over-exploration.

modules.name: Answer Aggregation Module
modules.description: Combine the refined sub-answers according to the logical structure specified in the plan (conjunction for multi-constraint queries, composition for sequential queries, union for multi-branch retrieval) to produce the final answer to the original question.

modules.name: Evaluation Metrics and Benchmark Runner
modules.description: Implement Hits@1 (Exact Match) accuracy computation with 95% confidence intervals over multiple seeds. Build benchmark evaluation pipelines for WebQSP, CWQ, and GrailQA, supporting both GPT-3.5 and GPT-4 as underlying LLMs, and reporting per-query-type breakdowns (compositional, conjunction, comparative, superlative, linear).

modules.name: Ablation Study Framework
modules.description: Implement controlled ablation experiments: (1) with/without self-refinement to measure error correction rate; (2) compare SPARQL-supervised planning module against general LLM planners (GPT-3.5, DeepSeek-R1) and different backbone sizes (Llama-3.2-1B, Llama-2-13B, Llama-3.1-8B) to isolate the contribution of structured planning supervision.

modules.name: Generalization and Efficiency Analysis
modules.description: Implement cross-KG generalization evaluation by running the full pipeline on both Freebase and WikiData schemas. Track and report computational efficiency metrics including number of LLM calls, input/output token counts, and total token usage per question. Compute FLOPs-accuracy trade-off curves by varying maximum planning iterations.

modules.name: Configuration Management and Result Reporting
modules.description: Manage experiment configurations (dataset, LLM backend, KG source, hyperparameters), log training and inference metrics, save/load planning module checkpoints, and generate automated result tables with mean ± confidence interval formatting for paper-ready reporting.
